ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: the input voltage u1 is applied between the upper and lower terminals on the left side; in the upper line, a resistor R is connected in series; the node at the right end of the resistor is connected to the output terminal on the right side, and is connected to the bottom common node through capacitor C; voltage u2 is marked between the upper and lower terminals on the right side, therefore u2 is the voltage across capacitor C. Reasoning: this structure is an RC low-pass voltage-divider branch driven by u1, and the capacitor impedance ZC=1/(jωC). Therefore U2/U1=ZC/(R+ZC)=1/(1+jωRC). The phase angle of this transfer function is -arctan(ωRC), which is a negative value, so u2 lags in phase relative to u1.

method.method_draft: Identify from the image that u2 is the capacitor voltage in an RC low-pass branch driven by u1 through R. Write the voltage divider using ZC=1/(jωC): U2/U1=ZC/(R+ZC)=1/(1+jωRC). Since the argument of this ratio is negative, conclude that u2 lags u1.

method.method_draft: Treat the circuit as a single series current charging the shunt capacitor through R. Take u2 as the capacitor voltage. The capacitor current leads u2 by 90°, and the resistor drop is in phase with that current. Adding the resistor drop to u2 gives the applied input voltage u1, whose phasor is advanced relative to u2. Therefore u2 is lagging relative to u1.
